probe.text_sample: Your Page Title Trendspotter Tools Categories Lists Blog Submit a tool Overview Buy Trendspotter Tools Categories Lists Blog Submit a tool Overview Buy Trendspotter Penna or Tinta: which writing assistant to pay for Two good writing tools that solve different problems. Here is how to pick. Elin Bergqvist 6 October 2026 Writing Penna and Tinta both help you write, and both cost about the same. After a month with each, the choice comes down to what you write most. Penna is for editing Penna reads what you already wrote and suggests changes that keep your voice. It is best on emails, posts and short pieces where you know what you want to say and need it tighter. Tinta is for long drafts Tinta starts from an outline and builds a long first draft for reports and proposals. It is slower and asks more questions, but the drafts need less rewriting than anything else we tried. If you can only pay for one Pick Penna if most of your writing is short and frequent. Pick Tinta if you write two or three long documents a month. Several of us use Penna daily and open Tinta only when a proposal is due.
